Step–1 : Nitration of toluene  
Toluene is an o-,p- directing substrate. In mixed nitric/sulfuric acid the major mono-nitration product is p-nitrotoluene.

        CH3–C6H5   --HNO3 / H2SO4-->   O2N–C6H4–CH3     (1)
                                p-Nitrotoluene

Step–2 : Oxidation of the benzylic methyl group  
Manganese dioxide in acidic medium oxidises a benzylic –CH3 first to an aldehyde (much faster than to a carboxylic acid). Hence

        O2N–C6H4–CH3  --MnO2 / H2SO4-->  O2N–C6H4–CHO   (2)
                               p-Nitrobenzaldehyde

Step–3 : Aldol (Claisen–Schmidt) condensation with acetone  
Under basic conditions acetone (which possesses two α-hydrogens) condenses with two equivalents of an aromatic aldehyde to give a “dibenzalacetone” type product. Thus

  2 O2N–C6H4–CHO  +  CH3–CO–CH3  --NaOH/aq, acetone-->  
                  O2N–C6H4–CH=CH–CO–CH=CH–C6H4–NO2 (3)
         (E,E)-1,5-bis(4-nitrophenyl)pent-1,4-dien-3-one  
         (4,4'-dinitro-dibenzalacetone)

Symmetry of 3  
• The entire π-conjugated framework (two p-nitrophenyl rings, the two C=C double bonds and the C=O group) lies in one plane; the nitro groups are also planar with the rings.  
• Reflection in this molecular plane leaves every atom in an equivalent position: the molecule possesses a single mirror plane σ.  
• There is no two-fold (C₂) rotational axis because a 180° rotation would interchange the carbonyl oxygen with empty space.  
• There is no inversion centre, no three-fold axis, and no set of three perpendicular C₂ axes.

Hence the only symmetry elements present are the identity E and one mirror plane σ → point group Cs.

Therefore the molecular symmetry group of compound 3 is Cs.

Answer: D
